body: Healthcare delivery in underserved rural regions faces systemic barriers: a severe shortage of medical professionals, fragmented communication, and geographical isolation. Foundation for Innovations in Health (FIH) is a not-for-profit social impact enterprise operating out of Kolkata, working to mitigate Multi-Dimensional Poverty (MDP) and build rural resilience through twin interventions — employment-oriented education for rural youth, and improved access to public health and primary care for last-mile communities. Its unifying purpose: "Health for a billion."

Studio 1947 was brought in to engineer a modern, highly accessible digital platform and headless content ecosystem. Our goal was to articulate FIH's transformative mission, empower rural youth and female health workers, and build institutional trust for corporate CSR and academic partnerships.

sections.heading: Strategic Context & The Rural Health Gap

sections.label: The Frontlines
body: The Sundarbans — the world's largest delta and mangrove forest — is FIH's proving ground. Spanning 9,630 sq. km across 102 islands (54 of them inhabited), it is home to more than 4.4 million people, many living in extreme isolation with limited access to essential services. The region sits on the frontlines of climate change: cyclones such as Amphan, Yaas, Fani and Bulbul have caused widespread devastation — loss of lives, large-scale displacement, and economic damage of nearly USD 20 billion — while rising sea levels, salinity and tidal flooding intensify poverty and disrupt public health.
Communicating complex, field-tested healthcare methodologies requires more than a static brochure site. FIH needed a digital flagship that could accomplish three critical objectives simultaneously:

cards.title: Institutional Trust
cards.body: Instilling visual confidence for major CSR donors, government partners, and academic institutions like IIT Kharagpur and NIT Meghalaya.

cards.title: Frugal Tech Showcase
cards.body: Demonstrating how digital clinics, the floating healthcare boat, and clinical decision-support software operate on the ground.

cards.title: Dynamic Operations
cards.body: Empowering non-technical field staff to publish real-time notifications, event updates, and healthcare stories effortlessly.

sections.heading: The Core Methodology: The 3T Model
sections.label: Proprietary Healthcare Framework
body: At the heart of FIH's operations is its proprietary 3T Model — a scalable strategy engineered to solve the shortage of doctors in remote communities. We translated this methodology into an intuitive, interactive visual breakdown on the digital platform:

cards.title: Employment-Oriented Education
cards.body: Training rural youth and women to become certified allied health professionals and frontline health workers.

cards.title: Frontline Empowerment
cards.body: Shifting specific primary-health tasks from overburdened doctors to trained community workers, bringing care directly to the doorstep.

cards.title: Frugal Health-Tech
cards.body: Deploying data-driven diagnostic tools, digital clinics, and clinical decision-support software tailored for low-resource settings.

sections.heading: Uday — Doctor at the Doorstep
sections.label: The Digital Clinic Model
body: "Uday" — doctor at the doorstep is FIH's model of digital clinic, delivering primary care and public health services to underserved rural populations through 15 centres (fixed and cycle-based mobile) in Birbhum district, West Bengal, and one motor-boat in the Sundarbans. It is led by remote doctors, delivered by community health workers (CHWs), and supported by two sets of innovative technologies: a clinical algorithm-driven Electronic Health Record (FIH's own copyrighted software) and clinical-grade diagnostic devices from IIT Kharagpur's Common Research & Technology Development Hub.

A single-visit, one-stop episode of care — consultation, tests, medicines, physiotherapy, injections and dressing — costs an average of Rs. 250, and the platform is engineered for ultra-low-bandwidth environments with high scalability. The site walks readers through the complete cycle of care in five steps:
list: Clinical Data Entry — the CHW records patient data as directed by the software algorithm triggered by the symptom.
Real-Time Sharing — history and examination data are shared with the remote doctor in real time.
Remote Consultation — the doctor reviews the data, consults the patient over video, records advice and shares it with the CHW.
Medical Action — the CHW undertakes tests and dispenses medicines as advised, sharing reports with the doctor in real time.
Documentation — the patient receives a printed prescription signed by the doctor, along with a follow-up appointment where required.

sections.heading: The Floating Digital Clinic
sections.label: Special Project Spotlight
body: To bridge the healthcare gap in the Sundarbans, FIH introduced the Floating Digital Clinic — a purpose-modified, fully equipped medical boat that travels across six remote islands, delivering accessible primary healthcare directly to underserved communities. Onboard, professionally certified health workers trained from local SC/ST communities deliver essential care, supported by real-time consultations with qualified doctors and specialists through the digital platform.

Beyond service delivery, the model creates local employment, builds community capacity, and strengthens resilience in one of the most climate-vulnerable regions in the world — a story the platform tells through immersive photography and field reports.

sections.heading: Digital Architecture & Interface Design
sections.label: Engineering & Technology
body: To deliver a lightning-fast, resilient experience, Studio 1947 built the flagship application using Next.js 16 (App Router), Tailwind CSS v4, and Sanity CMS. The system provides real-time content synchronization, responsive accessibility, and zero-latency page transitions — including a live notification bell that surfaces field updates straight from the CMS.

cards.title: Real-time Notification Bell & Lightbox
cards.body: A custom client notification bell fetching live Sanity CMS data, unread-state persistence via localStorage, and high-res image lightboxes for urgent field updates.

cards.title: Floating Digital Clinics & Stories
cards.body: Immersive media showcases highlighting the mobile clinic boat, cancer screening initiatives, and rural health worker training stories.

cards.title: CSR & 80G Tax-Exempt Information Hub
cards.body: A clear showcase of corporate CSR partnership frameworks, academic collaborations (IIT Kharagpur, NIT Meghalaya), and Section 80G tax-exemption compliance guidelines for prospective donors.

cards.title: Micro-Animations & Accessible Typography
cards.body: Motion-driven scroll reveals (Framer Motion) paired with high-legibility Google Fonts (Poppins for headings, Lato for body) for inclusive reading.

sections.heading: Recognition & Institutional Partnerships
sections.label: Proof of Trust
body: FIH's model has earned recognition that the platform surfaces prominently to build donor and partner confidence — including a Stanford University listing among the top 40 global changemakers, an MoU engaging FIH as 'Skill and Knowledge Partner' for the Allied Health Professional program at the IIT Kharagpur teaching hospital, and an MoU with NIT Meghalaya and DOT Inc. (Seoul) to train 15 visually impaired individuals as software programmers.
list: Stanford University — FIH's work recognized among the top 40 global changemakers.
IIT Kharagpur — MoU engaging FIH as Skill and Knowledge Partner for AHP education at the IIT KGP teaching hospital.
NIT Meghalaya — MoU with DOT Inc. (Seoul) to train visually impaired individuals as software programmers.
CSR partners — Mahanagar Gas Limited (330 youth as General Duty Assistants), Balmer Lawrie (Uday — Healthcare at the Doorstep), Essel Mining (mobile dental van), Ambuja Neotia (floating clinic).

sections.heading: Client Impact & Outcomes
sections.label: Measuring Success
list: 15 digital clinics + 1 floating clinic: a documented model of care at a single-visit average cost of Rs. 250 per episode.

Real livelihoods: placed graduates now work at Apollo Hospitals (Chennai), Tata Medical Centre (Kolkata), Cloud Nine (Vashi, Bangalore), and Ratna Memorial (Pune) — with salaries up to Rs. 20,000/month.
Empowered field staff: real-time publishing of health camps, emergency alerts, and training outcomes via Sanity CMS without developer intervention.
Accelerated partnerships: strengthened corporate CSR engagement and academic collaboration visibility for long-term health initiative funding.
